battle.name: 陳平章大寶叛亂
battle.brief: 禎明元年三月，前豐州刺史、曾任中護軍的章大寶在鬱林郡豐州舉兵反陳，州內義軍主陳景詳起兵討之，約七十日內擒斬叛首，首級傳回建康。卡面羅馬方陣盾並不在這場戰役，它是前100年前後的羅馬軍備，只能與陳朝步卒所倚的弩、槊、環首刀分作兩個技術譜系來看。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 這場叛亂發生在陳朝末年南疆的一個州裏，交戰雙方實力懸殊：叛方是解職之後仍握有舊部的地方將領章大寶，鎮方則是陳朝朝廷與豐州本地的官軍及義軍。陳朝自557年受梁禪建立，定都建康，禎明元年即585年，疆域以長江以南為主，與北面的隋朝隔大江、淮水一線對峙。陳朝的武備體系分兩層：京師建康的宿衛禁軍由中護軍統轄，中護軍是梁陳兩朝掌宮禁宿衛的最高武職，多由宗室或宿將出任；地方則由各州刺史兼領軍政，郡置太守、縣置令，兵員除正籍軍戶，還有按戶口徵發的鄉兵與鄉里自保的義軍。章大寶以中護軍之資外放豐州刺史，旋遭免職，於是以「前豐州刺史」的名號在州境內起兵，部眾主要來自他舊日軍府屬曲、州縣吏員與鄉里豪強。鎮方那邊，豐州義軍主陳景詳率鄉兵合圍州境叛軍，官軍隨後奉詔會剿；同年對岸的隋朝正是開皇五年，國力方盛，四年後便南下滅陳，因此這場叛亂不過是陳朝內部崩解的一個局部徵候。
countriesEn: This mutiny broke out in a single prefecture in the far southern reaches of the late Chen state, and the two sides were never remotely matched. The rebel side was a provincial commander who had lost his post but still held his old troops, Zhang Dabao. The side that crushed him was the Chen court together with the county administration and the locally raised volunteers of Fengzhou. The Chen had been founded in 557 on the abdication of the Liang, with the capital at Jiankang; Zhìmíng, its first year, is 585, and the state held most of the country south of the Yangtze, facing the Sui to the north across the great river and the Huai. Chen's military establishment had two layers. At Jiankang the palace guard was commanded by the zhonghujun, the highest office for the imperial guards in the Liang and Chen, normally held by a prince of the imperial clan or by a seasoned commander; in the provinces, military administration went with the office of governor, with a commandery magistrate and a county magistrate below, and the troops came from registered military households, from levies assessed on the population, and from village self-defence bands organised as yijun. Zhang Dabao was sent out to Fengzhou as governor while still holding the post of zhonghujun, was removed soon afterwards, and then raised men inside the prefecture under the style of former governor of Fengzhou; his following came chiefly from the officers of his old command, the county staff and the local landed families. Against him, Chen Jingxiang, the volunteer leader of Fengzhou, closed in with the village militia while imperial troops were ordered to join the pursuit; in the same year the Sui court across the river was in the fifth year of the Kaihuang era, at the height of its strength, and it would sweep south and destroy the Chen four years later, so this mutiny was only a local symptom of the disintegration working inside the Chen state.
people: 叛首章大寶是陳朝將領，先後任仁武將軍、豐州刺史，後升中護軍掌京師宿衛，再由中護軍外放豐州刺史，去職之後被追稱為「前豐州刺史」。他以舊部與州中吏民為骨幹起兵，兵鋒指向本州州城與周邊縣鎮。題名中的陳平屬陳氏宗室一系，其名在《陳書》《南史》未見專傳，只在部分戰爭列表中與章大寶並列；可以確定的是，禎明元年陳氏宗室在朝中分量仍重，同期朝廷以新除翊前將軍晉安王陳伯恭為安南將軍、湘州刺史，以新除翊左將軍永陽王陳伯智為尚書僕射，又令中護軍章大寶外放豐州刺史，宗室與掌兵將領在同一份人事安排裏交替升降，這正是叛亂得以發生的政治土壤。鎮壓方的主要人物是豐州義軍主陳景詳，他率鄉里武裝迅速合圍，在叛軍立足未穩之際擒斬章大寶，將首級送至建康，是這場戰爭唯一的勝負手。君主是陳後主陳叔寶，於582年冬即位，禎明元年尚在位；四年後隋軍南下，陳朝覆亡，他降隋後封鄭王，卒於隋開皇十九年。
peopleEn: The rebel leader Zhang Dabao was a Chen general who served in turn as general of the Renwu rank and governor of Fengzhou, was then advanced to zhonghujun in charge of the palace guard at the capital, and was sent out from that post to govern Fengzhou; after being dismissed he was referred to as the former governor of Fengzhou. He raised his men on the backbone of his old command and the county staff and populace, and pointed them at the prefectural seat itself and at the surrounding county towns. The name Chen Ping in the title belongs to a scion of the Chen imperial clan; no separate biography of him survives in the Book of Chen or the History of the Southern Dynasties, and he appears alongside Zhang Dabao only in certain lists of wars. What can be established is that princes of the clan still carried great weight at court in the first year of Zhìmíng: the court simultaneously promoted the newly appointed zhiqian general, Prince of Jinan Chen Bogong, to general of Annan and governor of Xiangzhou, the newly appointed zhiyou general, Prince of Yongyang Chen Bozhi, to vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and sent the zhonghujun Zhang Dabao out to Fengzhou. Royals and commanders rose and fell in the same arrangement of appointments, and that was the political soil in which the mutiny could take root. The decisive figure on the suppressing side was Chen Jingxiang, the volunteer leader of Fengzhou, who moved the village militia to close in quickly and cut Zhang Dabao down while the rebels had barely settled on their ground, then sent the head to Jiankang; he was the single turning point of the whole affair. The sovereign was Chen Shubao, Emperor Hou of Chen, who had taken the throne in the winter of 582 and was still reigning in the first year of Zhìmíng; four years later the Sui armies came south, the Chen fell, and after surrendering to the Sui he was made Prince of Zheng and died in the nineteenth year of the Kaihuang era.
kits: 卡面那面羅馬方陣盾是共和國晚期羅馬步兵的標誌裝備：直立微凸的長方木盾，外蒙皮革，中央鑄一枚鐵盾臍，高約一公尺、寬六七十公分，份量不輕，羅馬人靠它把整排士兵連成一堵可以互咬的盾牆，取勝靠的是盾緣相接而不是盾體多厚。不過要老實說：這面盾與585年陳朝的戰役毫無關係，它是前100年前後的羅馬軍備，比這場叛亂早了近七百年，只能當作對照件來用。陳朝步卒實際裝備的是另一套：長柄槊與矛、漢晉以來南方常見的環首刀、皮甲與札甲，以及漆木圓盾；投射火力才是陳軍的長項，蹶張弩、臂弩與車弩在守城與野戰都大量使用，江防還倚賴大艦與弩台。攻城與守城器械包括牛皮包覆的拍竿、撞車、巢車與望樓、石砲與飛石，竹木鹿角與拒馬用來封閉通道；水軍有艓艟、斗艦一類的內河戰船，隋人在後來造出的五牙大艦已是同一技術世代的頂點。叛軍這邊裝備更簡陋，多為竹木、雜械與漁獵工具，鄉兵步卒甚至沒有成制的皮甲。兩相比較，羅馬靠盾群結陣換推進力，陳朝靠弩與城牆換拒止力，這正是兩套防禦哲學的分野。
kitsEn: The scutum on the card is the signature piece of the equipment of the late Republican Roman infantry: an upright, slightly convex rectangle of timber faced with leather, with a wrought-iron boss at its centre, roughly a metre tall and sixty to seventy centimetres wide and heavy enough to be a burden. The Romans used it to lock a whole rank of men into a single wall of shields, winning by interlocking the edges rather than by the thickness of the boards. It must be said plainly, however, that this shield had nothing to do with the fighting in the Chen state in 585. It is Roman kit of about 100 BC, nearly seven centuries earlier than this mutiny, and can only serve as a point of comparison. The equipment of the Chen foot soldier was a different set altogether: long-hafted spears and pikes, ring-pommel swords common in the south since the Han and Jin, leather and lamellar armour, and lacquered wooden round shields. Missile fire was the real strength of the Chen army, and large crossbows, handbows and carriage crossbows were used in quantity both in the field and on the walls, with capital ships and bolt-shooting platforms forming the river defence. Siege and defence plant included hide-covered beating poles, battering carts, siege towers and observation platforms, stone-throwing engines and hand-thrown stones, with wooden abatis and cheval-de-frise used to close approaches. The navy had river craft of the lumu and doupan classes, and the five-tooth capital hulls the Sui later built were the summit of the same technical generation. The rebels were far worse equipped, with bamboo, oddments and fishing and hunting gear, and the village levies had not even standardised leather kit. Set the two side by side: Rome bought forward motion with shield walls, the Chen bought refusal with the crossbow and the city wall, and that is the divide between two different defensive philosophies.
tactics: 陳朝在開戰前的形勢已經對任何一支叛軍不利：州郡調兵需要尚書省下符，沒有符信的武裝在法理上只是「賊」，所以官軍與義軍鎮壓叛亂不必等待朝廷詔令就能集結。章大寶起兵在三月辛酉，憑的是州內舊部與鄉里的支持，火力以弩與散兵為主，一旦離開州境就失去補給線與援兵；實際上他也沒有越出豐州一步，說明這場叛亂從一開始就只是州級的內亂，目標是重掌本州兵柄，而非問鼎京師。陳景詳的處置相當簡潔：義軍先以熟悉地形的鄉里之人堵住縣道與渡口，把叛軍釘在有限的方圓之內，再集中兵力完成一次短促的攻擊，斬章大寶、傳首京師，不作攻城持久戰，也不打算擴張戰線。整個過程的補給靠州郡倉儲、縣城積粟與鬱江水路：從鬱林經西江、北江、湘水轉入長江直達建康，首級正是沿這條水路北運。同一時期的陳朝大戰術仍是據江防守、弩兵居城、器械壓制，章大寶這場叛亂正好反證：一旦內部的兵權與號令出了問題，龐大的防線會從內部鬆開。
tacticsEn: The situation the Chen state was in before the fighting began was already bad for any rebel army: to move troops between prefectures and commanderies required the Department of State Affairs to issue a warrant, and an armed band without such a warrant was legally nothing but a band of robbers, so the officials and the village volunteers could concentrate against the mutiny without waiting for an imperial order. Zhang Dabao raised his men on the eighth day of the third month, relying on old retainers inside the prefecture and on the countryside, with crossbows and loose troops as his main strength; once he left the prefecture he would have lost both his supply line and any hope of reinforcement, and in fact he never took a single step beyond Fengzhou, which shows from the outset that this was a prefectural mutiny aimed at regaining the command of his own province rather than at the capital. Chen Jingxiang's handling was deliberately simple: the volunteers first used men who knew the ground to close the county roads and the fords, pinning the rebels inside a small area, and then concentrated for one short, sharp attack that cut Zhang Dabao down and sent his head to Jiankang. There was no protracted siege, no attempt to widen the theatre. Supply throughout came from prefectural and command granaries, from grain stored in the county towns, and from the Yujiang waterway: from Yulin by the Xijiang, Beijiang and Xiangjiang into the Yangtze and on to Jiankang, and it was along this route that the head was carried north. The great tactical formula of the Chen at the time remained the same in any case: hold the river, put the crossbowmen on the walls, and let the engines do the pressing. The Zhang Dabao mutiny proves the reverse of that formula, that when command and authority fail inside, a vast defence line comes apart from within.
data: 可考的時間點很清楚：禎明元年即585年三月辛酉，前豐州刺史章大寶在豐州舉兵；夏四月庚戌，豐州義軍主陳景詳斬章大寶，傳首京師。由三月的辛酉到四月的庚戌，前後約七十日。陳朝立國於557年，至589年隋滅陳，共歷三十三年，禎明元年是陳後主在位的第三年（582年冬即位，尚不足三年），同時對應北面隋文帝的開皇五年。建康到鬱林郡豐州，水路要經鬱江、西江、北江、湘水再入長江，逾二千里，首級北運即循此線。制度面上，陳朝京畿宿衛由中護軍所領，地方軍權歸各州刺史，調兵須憑符信；地方義軍沒有固定員額，陳景詳所領的豐州義軍史書只記「義軍主」三字，未載人數兵械，所以這支部眾的規模只能從它能在數十日內完成一次擒斬行動去推想，不能給出確數。陳朝全境州郡總數與當年兵戶數，在這件事上並無可核對的記載，撰述者不宜代為估算。
dataEn: The datable points are clear. In the first year of Zhìmíng, 585, on the eighth day of the third month, the former governor of Fengzhou Zhang Dabao rose in revolt at Fengzhou; in the fourth month, on the day gengxu, the volunteer leader of Fengzhou Chen Jingxiang cut Zhang Dabao down and carried his head to the capital. From the xinyou day of the third month to the gengxu day of the fourth month is about seventy days. The Chen was founded in 557 and lasted thirty-three years until the Sui destroyed it in 589; the first year of Zhìmíng was the third year of the reign of Emperor Hou of Chen, who had taken the throne in the winter of 582 and had not yet completed three years on it, and it corresponds to the fifth year of the Kaihuang era of the Sui emperor to the north. From Jiankang to Fengzhou commandery in Yulin the water route runs by the Yujiang, the Xijiang, the Beijiang and the Xiangjiang before entering the Yangtze, well over two thousand li, and it was this line the head travelled along northwards. Institutionally, the metropolitan guard was under the zhonghujun, military authority in the provinces went to the governors, and troops could not be moved without a warrant. The local volunteer bands had no fixed establishment: for the Fengzhou band under Chen Jingxiang the histories record only the three characters for volunteer leader, with neither numbers nor equipment, so the size of that force can only be inferred from the fact that it carried out a capture and execution within a few dozen days, and no firm figure should be given. The total number of prefectures and commanderies of the Chen and the military households of the year leave no verifiable record in connection with this affair, and it would be improper for a writer to supply an estimate.
cause: 起事的前因可以分三層看。第一層是陳朝本身的政治氣候：陳宣帝晚年多忌，誅除宗室與功臣的例子不少，陳後主即位後寵信近臣、營建宮觀，民間轉向佛教而租役照舊，士人對朝廷的信任在下降。第二層是章大寶個人的處境：他以中護軍掌京師宿衛，位望不低，卻被外放到鬱林郡所屬的豐州當刺史，隨即又被免職，「前豐州刺史」這個稱呼本身就是一次貶抑的記錄；掌握過禁軍又被打發到邊州的人，若自認還能號召舊部，這種落差就足以變成反心。第三層是外面的壓力：同年北面的隋朝正值開皇盛期，南方則傳出隋使招降、境內人望觀望的訊息，陳朝宗室與將領之間的互信被這些消息削弱。題名中的陳平代表的是宗室一端的不安，關於他的具體事蹟，現存史籍未立專傳，只能確定禎明元年前後陳氏宗室在朝中仍居要位、與掌兵將領交替升降，而叛亂正是發生在這樣的縫隙裏。
causeEn: The background to the rising can be read in three layers. The first is the political weather inside the Chen state itself: the last years of Emperor Xuan of Chen were marked by suspicion, and not a few princes and meritorious officials were put to death; after Emperor Hou took the throne he favoured courtiers and building projects, the population turned increasingly to Buddhism while the tax and corvée load was unchanged, and the confidence of the scholar class in the court declined. The second is Zhang Dabao's own position: he had commanded the palace guard at Jiankang as zhonghujun, a station of no mean rank, yet he was packed off to govern Fengzhou in Yulin commandery and very soon dismissed, and the style former governor of Fengzhou is itself the record of a demotion. A man who has held the guard and then been sent to a frontier prefecture, and who still believes he can call up his old men, has a gap of that kind easily enough turn into a revolt. The third layer is the pressure from outside: in the same year the Sui to the north was in the full strength of the Kaihuang era, while in the south there were reports of Sui envoys seeking surrender and of people watching to see which way the wind blew, and messages of that kind wore away the trust between the Chen princes and their commanders. The Chen Ping of the title stands for the unease on the princely side; the surviving histories give him no separate biography, and all that can be established is that princes of the clan still held high posts in the first year of Zhìmíng, rising and falling in alternation with the commanders of troops, and that the mutiny grew precisely in such a gap.
impact: 直接結果是陳朝中央的威信靠一次地方平叛重新確認：章大寶的首級送到建康，朝廷以此昭示叛逆者的下場，豐州義軍首領陳景詳則論功行賞，州境秩序很快恢復。更深一層的影響在制度面：這場叛亂說明陳朝中護軍與州刺史兩個位置上的人並未真正被朝廷掌握，把禁軍資歷者外放州郡的做法本身製造了「前刺史」這種可以據州自立的角色，與此前晉安陳寶應據郡自據的舊例相呼應。對歷史走向而言，這只是一場被迅速壓下去的局部叛亂，對陳朝的國運沒有直接改變；但它發生在陳後主治下最敏感的年月，四年後的589年，隋軍南下，陳後主在采石、姑孰一線的江防崩潰後出降建康，陳氏宗室與大批官員被移往關中，陳朝三十三年的基業就此終結，陳後主後來在隋朝封鄭王，於開皇十九年死於洛陽。一場州級叛亂的最後意義，也許就在於它是陳朝末年最便宜的一次警鐘，而朝堂沒有聽。
impactEn: The immediate effect was that the authority of the Chen court was reasserted by a local suppression: the head of Zhang Dabao was brought to Jiankang and displayed to show the fate of rebels, the volunteer leader of Fengzhou Chen Jingxiang was rewarded for his service, and order inside the prefecture was restored quickly. At a deeper level the consequences were institutional: the mutiny showed that men holding the posts of zhonghujun and provincial governor were not truly in the court's grasp, and the practice of sending men with guard experience out to govern prefectures itself created the type of former governor who could hold a prefecture on his own, echoing the earlier precedent of Chen Baoying, who had occupied Jinan on his own authority. As history it was a local rising put down quickly, with no direct effect on the fortunes of the state. Yet it came in the most sensitive years of Emperor Hou's reign, and four years later, in 589, the Sui armies came south, the river defences along the Caishi and Gushu lines collapsed, Emperor Hou surrendered at Jiankang, the princes of the Chen clan and a great part of the official class were moved to Guanzhong, and the thirty-three year foundation of the Chen came to an end. The deposed emperor was later made Prince of Zheng under the Sui and died in Luoyang in the nineteenth year of the Kaihuang era. The last meaning of a prefectural mutiny may be that it was the cheapest warning bell of the late Chen, and that the court did not listen to it.
result: 起兵到覆滅，前後約七十日。章大寶的叛軍未能越出豐州境，陳景詳率豐州義軍迅速合圍，完成一次短促的攻擊，將章大寶斬首，首級傳至建康，叛亂在州級層面即告終結。朝廷的軍政體系沒有為此投入大規模的野戰兵員，說明陳朝地方仍保有相當的自我鎮壓能力，也說明這場衝突從來沒有升級為內戰。叛首伏誅、州境復平，陳景詳以義軍首功受賞，成為這場戰爭中唯一留下姓名的鎮壓方人物；而題名所列的另一端，陳平在文獻中的痕跡極淡，只能作為宗室中同類不安的注腳處理。結果層面還要加一條長尾：陳朝並未因這場叛亂而改弦更張，四年後大隋的軍隊越過大江，宿衛與州軍系統在崩潰中一起瓦解，陳後主出降，陳氏政權的終局由此確定，而章大寶在585年春天的那次起事，只是這條長尾前端的一小節。
resultEn: From the rising to its end, about seventy days. The rebel army of Zhang Dabao never got outside the borders of Fengzhou. Chen Jingxiang, leading the volunteers of Fengzhou, closed in quickly and completed a single short attack that cut Zhang Dabao down; the head was carried to Jiankang and the mutiny was over at prefectural level. The military and administrative apparatus of the court committed no large field army to it, which shows that the localities of the Chen still retained a considerable capacity to put down disorder on their own, and equally that the conflict never escalated into civil war. The rebel chief was executed, the prefecture was quiet again, and Chen Jingxiang was rewarded as the leading volunteer of the affair, leaving him the only person of the suppressing side whose name survives. At the other end of the title, the trace of Chen Ping in the literature is very faint and can only be handled as a footnote on the same sort of unease among the imperial clan. There is a longer tail to the outcome as well: the Chen did not mend its ways because of this mutiny, and four years later the armies of the great Sui crossed the great river, the guard and the provincial armies came apart together in the collapse, Emperor Hou surrendered, and the end of the Chen was settled. The rising of Zhang Dabao in the spring of 585 was only a small section at the front end of that long tail.
